slot.brief: Show an alkene structure in a figure; give the ozonolysis product(s) and ask which alkene would produce them.

stem: The alkene shown in the figure undergoes reductive ozonolysis ($\text{O}_3$ followed by $\text{Zn} / \text{H}_2\text{O}$). What are the resulting organic products?

verdicts.working: Figure shows CH3–C(CH3)=CH–CH3 (2-methylbut-2-ene). Reductive ozonolysis cleaves the C=C: the disubstituted carbon gives (CH3)2C=O (propan-2-one) and the CH–CH3 carbon gives CH3CHO (ethanal).

working:
The alkene shown in the figure is 2-methylbut-2-ene, with structural formula $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$.

Reductive ozonolysis cleaves the carbon-carbon double bond and replaces it with carbonyl groups ($=\text{O}$):
$$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow[\text{Zn}/\text{H}_2\text{O}]{\text{O}_3} (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{O} + \text{O}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$$

The products are propan-2-one (acetone) and ethanal (acetaldehyde).

figure.description: Skeletal structure of 2-methylbut-2-ene: a 4-carbon chain (but-2-ene) with a double bond between C2 and C3, and a single methyl substituent attached to C2.
